name: Nadab
bio:
Nadab is Aaron's firstborn son, who along with his brother Abihu and seventy elders of Israel was called up Mount Sinai, bowing down to God from a distance and being granted the rare privilege of "seeing the God of Israel" and eating and drinking in His presence (Exodus 24:1, 9-11).

However, just as the tabernacle was completed and the priesthood had begun, Nadab and Abihu each took their own censer, put fire and incense in it, and offered "strange fire" before the LORD — fire He had not commanded. Fire went out from the LORD and consumed them, and they died before Him (Leviticus 10:1-2). Moses told Aaron, "This is it that the LORD spake, saying, I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified" — and Aaron was silent. Moses then had Aaron's cousins Mishael and Elzaphan carry the bodies outside the camp, and strictly forbade Aaron and his surviving sons Eleazar and Ithamar from tearing their clothes or leaving their hair unkempt in mourning, lest they too die, leaving the rest of Israel to mourn the burning the LORD had kindled (Leviticus 10:3-7). The deaths of Nadab and Abihu stand as an important biblical warning about the seriousness of worshiping God on one's own terms rather than as He commands.
